key_findings.finding: The atom-mapped-like structures decode to Boc-protected (S)-2-amino-3-(4-chlorophenyl)propanoic acid and a secondary piperazine-containing fused N-heteroarene. The product is the corresponding carboxamide: the amino-acid C(=O)OH is converted to C(=O)N(piperazine), while the Boc group remains. Thus the newly formed bond is the carboxyl carbon–piperazine nitrogen bond; the acid OH (after activation, typically as an activated ester/acyl intermediate) is the leaving group-derived substituent.
